articles.detail: 5 cycles completed, avg 10 published/cycle (up from 58 yesterday)

experiment: Skipped — all four goals are met with margin, nothing was pending evaluation, and no noNewExperimentsUntil gate is set. The day's real defect is a fourth distinct duplicate shape (identical title, different source URLs, six days apart), which lives in scripts/lib/dedup.js and scripts/validate-articles.js — outside the tunable-parameter surface. No feed cap or selector floor would have caught it.
weakestArea: Regional balance is the softest metric that still passes: the Americas took 23 of 64 articles (36%) while Oceania fell to 1 and Europe halved from 19 to 7 overnight. But the genuine miss is again duplication that the counter reads as zero. Two articles now share the exact title "Experts Sell Their Judgment" — 2026-09-03 (Johannesburg, Rest of World) and 2026-09-09 (Shenzhen, Rest of World) — same outlet, same beat, different URLs and datelines, so every dedup layer passes them. A corpus scan finds 25 exact title collisions since 2026-06-01; roughly half are legitimate developing-story follow-ups, the rest are recaps that shipped twice. This is the fourth duplicate shape logged in four days, after same-URL (2026-09-07 ziltivekimab), same-title-from-different-clusters (2026-09-06 Nabatieh hospital) and same-event-across-categories (2026-09-08 Navier-Stokes).
watching: The Iran/Gulf war cluster took roughly ten of today's 64 articles — IAEA referral, aviation sanctions, strikes on Jordan and Bahrain, the Saudi refinery, Hormuz rerouting, migrant workers, Indian market exposure — distinct angles so far, but the single-event concentration is the highest this week.
Europe fell from 19 articles to 7 in one day while the Americas rose from 13 to 23; neither breaches a target, but the swing is larger than any day-over-day move this week.
Africa recovered from 4 to 10 and finally spans more than conflict — Ekiti rice farming, Lassa preparedness, Liberian fistula care, Lake Tana weed modelling.
Science rose to 12 and now draws on ten distinct outlets against yesterday's five, so the category no longer rests on Nature and STAT alone.
Freshness is computed on only 15 of 64 articles, a thinner base than yesterday's 21 of 58, so the 0.2 median is less well supported than it looks.

Both prior duplicate pairs are still live in content/articles/ — the 2026-09-07 ziltivekimab pair and the 2026-09-08 Navier-Stokes pair; three audits have now flagged the first and nothing has removed a copy.
coverageGaps: Oceania has 1 article, the lowest this week, and there is still no Pacific island coverage for a third consecutive day.
Europe's 7 articles are Saxony-Anhalt, the NATS outage and war-adjacent energy stories; no EU economic or regulatory thread at all.
Latin America appears only as Peru's tomb find and Rubio's Colombia trip — two isolated items, no sustained regional story.
Economy at 14 leans on markets and corporate filings (Florida insurer, LIV Golf, stablecoin pilots); no development-economics or trade-policy reporting outside the Hormuz rerouting angle.
context: The experiment slot has been free since 2026-05-26 and every goal has been met on consecutive audits, so parametric tuning has nothing to fix. The open work is structural and still needs an operator decision: the title-overlap layer in scripts/lib/dedup.js is gated to niche-only sources, which is why two mainstream Rest of World pieces republished under one title today, and scripts/validate-articles.js has no duplicate-title or duplicate-URL gate at all. Ungating the title layer for mainstream outlets and adding a title-collision check at validation would close all four shapes seen this week. Both files are outside the daily-tuning parameter surface. Three duplicate pairs remain live and unremoved.
